Cambridge Dictionary named "human" its word of the year for 2026, and AI is the reason.
Its lexicographer says AI is changing how we talk about being human.
"Agent" was on the shortlist, and "fear of becoming obsolete" is a phrase to watch next year.

paragraphs.text: Cambridge Dictionary named "human" its word of the year for 2026, the Associated Press reported on November 17, 2026. The AP said that fears about artificial intelligence led the dictionary to choose the word as the one that best captures the cultural mood of the year, describing the pick partly as a backlash against AI.

The adjective comes from the Latin humanus and has been in use since the 1450s, according to the AP. Cambridge defines it as having the qualities, faults and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals or machines.

Colin McIntosh, a lexicographer at Cambridge Dictionary, said in a statement that AI is changing how people talk about being human. According to the AP, he said fears about what people may lose when they outsource their thinking have led many to reconsider how much they rely on the technology.

Francesca Woodward, a board member at Cambridge University Press, said the word captured the zeitgeist of 2026, AFP reported. She said people had been considering what it is to be human, mainly because of fears that AI could take their jobs. The dictionary's lexicographers also noticed more use of compounds such as human-made and human author.

AFP reported that the selection is based on several criteria, including the words people search for on the Cambridge Dictionary website. It added that public figures including Pope Leo XIV, Bill Gates, Mary Beard and Cate Blanchett have taken part in the wider debate about AI and humanity. The AP quoted Gates, the Microsoft co-founder, as saying that AI is making people think harder about what it means to be human.

Tom McClelland, a philosopher of science at the University of Cambridge, called the pick an interesting choice, AFP reported. He said the understanding of humanity is changing and raised the question of what sets people apart, whether consciousness, creativity or compassion.
The shortlist and the words to watch

Other words considered for 2026 included "agent," which the dictionary defines as an AI system that can operate in a complicated way without human control. The AP also listed "analogue," used for experiences or objects that do not involve the internet or digital technology. AFP named "wholesome" and "dusking," the practice of watching daylight turn to darkness to relax.

New entries added in 2026 include "aura farming" and "looksmaxxing," according to AFP. Among the terms the dictionary expects to watch in 2027 is FOBO, short for fear of becoming obsolete because AI can do a person's job, along with "weather whiplash."

AI has shaped several recent words of the year. Cambridge chose "hallucinate" in 2023, referring to AI systems that make up information, and Collins picked "AI" the same year, the AP reported. Merriam-Webster chose "slop" for low quality AI content in 2025, Collins has picked "vibe coding," and Cambridge's 2025 word was "parasocial."

The choice of an ordinary, centuries old word says more about the year than a new coinage would. Earlier AI words of the year described what the technology does, such as hallucinating or producing slop. This one describes how people feel about it, with job security and reliance on chatbots at the center of that feeling.
FOBO is the term to watch: if fear of becoming obsolete keeps showing up in searches through 2027, it will be a measure of how worried ordinary workers remain about AI and their jobs.
